names.official: Independent State of Papua New Guinea

summary: Papua New Guinea gives a visa on arrival to a short list of countries — including the UK, Canada, Japan, Singapore, Indonesia, Israel and much of the Pacific — whose citizens can instead apply online in advance for a 60-day Easy Visitor Permit (no visa fee, USD 50 eVisa fee). Other nationalities apply for a visitor visa on the paper form before travel. Melanesian Spearhead Group neighbors get a 30-day visa on arrival.

vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required for travelers aged one year and over arriving from a country with risk of yellow fever transmission, including those who only transited through the airport of such a country, however short the transit.

vaccinations.name: Hepatitis A and routine vaccines
vaccinations.text: Not required for entry. Canada's travel health advice recommends hepatitis A vaccination for all travellers and up-to-date routine vaccines, which include tetanus, and says there is a risk of malaria in certain areas: see a travel health clinic about antimalarials, ideally 6 weeks before you go.

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read makes travel insurance a condition of entry to Papua New Guinea. onwardTicket.text: Visitor, Easy Visitor Permit and business visa applications must include a travel itinerary with a confirmed onward or return ticket, and Melanesian Spearhead Group visa-on-arrival travellers need one too.

proofOfFunds.text: Visitor and Easy Visitor Permit applicants must provide their itinerary and a guarantee that they are financially secure. No fixed amount is published.

declarations.name: PNG Digital Arrival Card (PNGDAC)
declarations.submitWindow: Online within 72 hours before arrival, and before check-in
declarations.text: Every traveller, including PNG citizens and permanent residents, must complete the PNG Digital Arrival Card online, within the 72 hours before arrival. ICSA has told airlines that travellers must complete it before a boarding pass is issued. It is not a visa.

source.name: PNG Immigration and Citizenship Services Authority — Mandatory completion of PNG Digital Arrival Card

currencyLimits.text: Travellers carrying currency or valuables worth PGK 20,000 or more must declare them on a Cross-Border Movement of Currency and Valuables (CMCV) form, available at all customs entry and exit points. faq.question: Do I need a visa for Papua New Guinea?
faq.answer: Yes, every foreign visitor needs a visa. Citizens of the countries on ICSA's visa-on-arrival list, including the UK, Canada, Japan, Singapore, Indonesia, Israel and much of the Pacific, can get one on arrival, and Fijian, Solomon Islands and Vanuatu citizens get a 30-day visa on arrival. The same visa-on-arrival nationalities can apply online in advance for the 60-day Easy Visitor Permit (no visa fee, USD 50 eVisa fee); everyone else, including US, Australian, New Zealand and EU citizens, applies for a visitor visa before travel.

faq.question: How do I apply for the PNG tourist eVisa?
faq.answer: ICSA's Visitor Visa page opens the eVisa portal to citizens of the countries on its visa-on-arrival list. For the Easy Visitor Permit, ICSA's guide asks for a request letter, a copy of your passport bio page, and your travel itinerary with a confirmed onward or return ticket and a guarantee that you are financially secure; the turnaround is 10 working days when all requirements are met. Other nationalities use the paper visitor-visa form.

faq.question: Is there a visa on arrival in Papua New Guinea?
faq.answer: Yes, for the countries on the visa-on-arrival list published by the Immigration and Citizenship Services Authority. The list includes the UK, Canada, Japan, Singapore, Indonesia, Israel, the United Arab Emirates and most Pacific Island states; mainland New Zealand, France and the United States are not eligible. Chinese ordinary passport holders qualify only in an organised tour group.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Papua New Guinea?
faq.answer: The 60-day Easy Visitor Permit is a single-entry stay of 60 days from arrival, and ICSA says a visitor visa is in most circumstances a single-entry stay of 60 days. Depending on the visa, ICSA says you may be able to extend your stay without leaving the country.

faq.question: Is Papua New Guinea safe to visit?
faq.answer: The UK Foreign Office says there is a high risk of serious crime in Port Moresby, Lae and Mount Hagen and that walking after dark is particularly dangerous in urban centres, and it advises against all but essential travel to Hela and Southern Highlands provinces and to Enga (except Wabag District) because of tribal fighting.

faq.question: What vaccinations do I need for Papua New Guinea?
faq.answer: A yellow fever certificate is required only if you arrive from, or transited through the airport of, a yellow fever risk country. Nothing else is compulsory. Canada's travel health advice recommends hepatitis A vaccination for all travellers and up-to-date routine vaccines, and says there is a risk of malaria in certain areas, so ask a travel health clinic about antimalarials.
